article.title: Tyre makers push through a 3% replacement-market price hike as carbon black costs bite
article.text: Leading Indian tyre manufacturers have raised replacement-market prices by about three per cent from this week, the first industry-wide increase in four quarters, after synthetic rubber and carbon black quotations rose sharply through the previous quarter. Replacement demand is roughly two-thirds of industry volumes and is far less price sensitive than the original-equipment channel, where contracts are annually negotiated and pass-through is slower. MRF and Apollo Tyres both confirmed the revision; CEAT declined to comment on pricing but said its raw-material basket had inflated in the high single digits. The hike restores part of the gross margin lost since the previous cycle rather than expanding it.
article.note: Price-hike stories are commonly mis-signed. The hike is margin RECOVERY against a cost already incurred, not a windfall -- and the peer that would not confirm must not be waved through on its neighbours' evidence.

universe.name: MRF
universe.business_desc: India's largest tyre manufacturer with the strongest replacement-market franchise and premium pricing power across truck and passenger radials.

universe.name: Apollo Tyres
universe.business_desc: Tyre manufacturer with Indian and European operations, consuming crude-derived synthetic rubber and carbon black as primary raw materials.

universe.name: CEAT
universe.business_desc: Tyre manufacturer with a two-wheeler and passenger-vehicle skew and a higher original-equipment share than its larger peers.

shocks.label: Tyre input costs
shocks.mechanism: Crude-derived synthetic rubber and carbon black form the largest share of tyre raw-material cost, and the announced price hike only partially recovers the inflation already booked

companies.name: MRF
companies.mechanism: The highest replacement-market mix in the industry means the three per cent hike reaches two-thirds of volumes immediately, recovering more of the carbon black inflation than peers can
companies.rationale: Strongest replacement franchise and demonstrated pricing power in truck radials
negative_channels: synthetic rubber and carbon black cost inflation

companies.name: Apollo Tyres
companies.mechanism: The hike recovers replacement margin at home while the European operation faces its own raw-material inflation without a matching pricing action, leaving the consolidated effect two-sided
companies.rationale: Split India and Europe operations with only the Indian channel repricing
offsetting_channels: domestic recovery offsets part of the European drag

companies.name: CEAT
companies.mechanism: Assumed participation in the industry-wide hike would lift realisation across the two-wheeler replacement channel by a similar three per cent
companies.rationale: Peer read-across from the two makers that did confirm the revision

ground_truth.rationale: The verifier accepted the two makers that confirmed the revision and stayed SILENT on the one that declined to comment. Silence is not acceptance: CEAT carries a peer-read-across rationale with no company-specific evidence and must not be published, even though its economics are entirely plausible and it will very likely follow the hike.
